versions.statuteQuote: (ii) the payment of the amount of damages that the landlord has suffered by reason of the tenant's noncompliance with § 55.1-1227, less reasonable wear and tear

summaryForModel: Deposit deductions for damage must exclude reasonable wear and tear. A lease that charges the tenant for normal wear and tear (such as routine repainting, carpet wear, or minor scuffs) conflicts with this.
paraphraseExamples: Tenant will be charged for repainting and carpet replacement upon move-out regardless of condition.
Normal wear and tear will be deducted from the security deposit.
A cleaning and carpet fee of $400 will be withheld from the deposit.
tenantExplanation: Your landlord can't take money from your deposit for normal wear from everyday living, only for damage beyond that.
action: You can ask your landlord to remove automatic move-out charges for normal wear. Take dated move-in photos to show what was already there.
